_comment: Fleet-wide registry of carried upstreams for scripts/check-plugin-drift.sh (HIMMEL-869/HIMMEL-1435). Covers the remaining shipped fleet and may deliberately overlap a detection surface when this registry supplies repair metadata: claude-obsidian is release-checked through plugin-upstreams.json AND declared here so the nightly fork-resync cadence can audit its rebase. Each entry names a TRUE upstream and how to detect that it has advanced past what himmel carries, so the goal state 'always sync + additive' (fork deltas stay strictly additive on a current upstream base) is observable. Two detection kinds, each a discriminated union on `kind`: (1) commit_head — compare a local commit to the tracked repo's default-branch HEAD. `mode: pin` takes the commit from `pinned_commit` (full or short SHA; short is resolved via gh). `mode: checkout` takes it from a local git checkout at `checkout_path` ($VAR/${VAR} expanded cross-platform by the script's python emitter; absent checkout -> UNCHECKED, never drift). Use `pin` for vendored copies (the dir is NOT a git checkout of upstream — claude-hud) and `checkout` for editable/installed git checkouts (hermes-agent). (2) tag_release — compare a local version to the tracked repo's latest STABLE version tag (highest semver via sort -V, prereleases excluded — same discipline as the claude-obsidian fork override). `mode: base` takes the version from `synced_base` (a recorded literal). `mode: probe` runs `version_command` (simple space-separated tokens) and extracts the version via `version_regex` (a pattern matching the bare version, e.g. `[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+[0-9A-Za-z.-]*`; no capture group — grep -oE prints the whole match). Use `probe` for installed binaries/CLIs whose version is only knowable by running them (rtk, twitter-cli). A `mode: base` entry MAY additionally declare `version_pin` — `{file, template}`, where `template` is a LITERAL string carrying a `{version}` placeholder that occurs EXACTLY ONCE in `file` (e.g. graphify's `GRAPHIFY_VERSION:-{version}` in scripts/lib/graphify-bin.sh). That field is what makes the entry AUTO-BUMPABLE by scripts/upstreams/apply-drift-bump.sh (the nightly drift-fix cadence, HIMMEL-1323): the bumper rewrites the in-repo pin literal and `synced_base` together, so the two can never diverge. A `mode: probe` entry has no in-repo pin at all — its drift is repaired by upgrading the INSTALLED tool on this machine, so it MAY instead declare `upgrade` — `{command, unattended, note}`, where `command` is an argv ARRAY (never a shell string: no shell means no injection surface) run from the repo root. `scripts/upstreams/apply-tool-upgrade.sh` runs it, then re-probes and requires the version to have STRICTLY advanced — a command that exits 0 without moving the version is a failure, not a success. `unattended` is the policy gate the nightly cadence enforces structurally: the cadence always passes `--unattended`, which refuses any entry not marked `unattended: true`, so a Tier B tool (rtk) keeps a working one-command upgrader while still requiring an operator to pull the trigger. An entry WITHOUT `version_pin` (base) or `upgrade` (probe) is reported SKIP (manual) and never touched — that is deliberate for qmd, whose in-repo pin is a fork SHA (`_qmd_fork_ref`), not a version: moving its `synced_base` alone would flip the guard to CURRENT while the fork sits unrebased, laundering the very signal the entry exists to raise. `tier` is informational only (A=proactive-adopt, B=reactive-adopt per the HIMMEL-850 audit) and appears in the guard's output so a reader can tell expected-churn (Tier B usually reads BEHIND by design) from a genuine stale pin. Installed marketplaces (caveman, obsidian-skills, openai-codex, claude-video, claude-plugins-official, ...) are NOT listed here: they are discovered dynamically from ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json (DRIFT_KNOWN_MARKETPLACES override) so the guard auto-covers any future marketplace install, each checked as a commit_head/checkout against its source repo. Registry forks (qmd and claude-obsidian) are mechanically rebased and delta-classified by resync-fork.sh; claude-obsidian is deliberately non-additive and its unattended audit stops without pushing. UPSTREAM_PIN vendored forks retain a manual file-level delta judgment — see the script header. The six luna-* rows cover third-party Obsidian plugin assets bundled in templates/luna-second-brain; they have no version_pin because repair is a reviewed re-vendor, so the nightly bump leg reports SKIP (manual) while detection remains automatic.

entries.name: claude-obsidian

fork.note: Nightly resync audit target. The marketplace pin is an installable fork tag, not a SHA, so resync-fork.sh resolves the tag to its commit and reports the rebased SHA; after operator review the fork tag must be re-cut and the marketplace ref updated. The carried delta modifies upstream files by design (removed hooks and locking patches), so a NON-ADDITIVE audit is expected and still useful; unattended cadence stops after the report and never pushes. synced_base deliberately duplicates scripts/plugin-upstreams.json and tests require equality.

entries.note: True fork yotamleo/claude-obsidian, installed from marketplace/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json at an immutable tag. Upstream release drift is also detected through scripts/plugin-upstreams.json; this row adds the fork-resync audit surface. Keep synced_base equal in both registries on every re-sync.

entries.name: hermes-agent
entries.note: Editable pip checkout (the multi-provider gateway). Tier B / high-churn (18k+ open PRs): reads BEHIND by design; that IS the signal — consult the HIMMEL-850 steal-list when a real bug hits. UNCHECKED if the checkout is absent on this machine (CI / fresh clone).

entries.name: rtk

upgrade.note: Operator APPROVED unattended rtk upgrades on 2026-07-28, overriding the Tier B default (this field, not the tier, is what the cadence reads). The prior reservation is recorded because it is the thing to revisit if rtk ever misbehaves: rtk is Tier B — BEHIND is normally its intended steady state — and the known git-diff rewrite bug HIMMEL-270 is still unfixed upstream, so chasing releases does not fix the bug that actually bites. What makes unattended acceptable anyway: upgrade-rtk.sh backs the binary up, smoke-tests the new one, and ROLLS BACK on failure; and the blast radius is low because scripts/hooks/rtk-hook-guard.sh is fail-OPEN — a broken rtk stops rewriting Bash commands rather than blocking them. Set this back to false to return rtk to operator-triggered.

entries.note: Installed binary at ~/.local/bin/rtk. Tier B (reactive); known git-diff rewrite bug HIMMEL-270 is NOT directly fixed upstream. UNCHECKED if rtk absent / --version yields no parseable version.

entries.name: twitter-cli

upgrade.note: PyPI package installed via `uv tool install`. Safe to run unattended: non-interactive, idempotent, no sudo, no remote-script-pipe-to-shell, and it resolves through uv rather than fetching a release artifact. Low blast radius too — twitter-cli is a plain subprocess call from marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/tools/twitter-cli-enrich.mjs, wired into no hook, so a regression breaks X-thread enrichment and nothing else. Tier A (proactive) with no known-bug caveat, so chasing releases is the declared stance.

entries.note: Installed CLI at ~/.local/bin/twitter (consumed by the telegram clipper). Tier A (proactive). UNCHECKED if twitter absent / --version yields no parseable version.

entries.name: graphify
entries.note: Upstream PyPI graphifyy, version-pinned in scripts/lib/graphify-bin.sh (_graphify_version). DE-FORKED from yotamleo/graphify in HIMMEL-1048 / issue #469: the fork carried ZERO delta over upstream (its only purpose — declaring the mcp dep, which upstream keeps optional — is handled by the `--with mcp` install flag), so himmel tracks upstream directly. tracked_repo is the TRUE upstream (Graphify-Labs). synced_base = the pinned upstream release. latest_source=release because upstream tags are NON-MONOTONIC: a stale v1.0.0 (2026-04) predates the current v0.9.x line, so highest-semver-tag would report a permanent phantom BEHIND; the Releases API returns the real latest. BEHIND here means: bump _graphify_version in graphify-bin.sh to the new release AND bump synced_base here (a one-line pair — no fork rebase). `version_pin` above declares where that in-repo literal lives, so scripts/upstreams/apply-drift-bump.sh applies BOTH halves mechanically; review happens on the resulting PR, not on hand-editing the two spots.

entries.name: cli-proxy-api
entries.note: CLIProxyAPI codex-lane proxy (HOST process on 127.0.0.1:8317; installed + run by scripts/setup/cli-proxy-lane.ps1). Added to the nightly drift machinery (HIMMEL-1451) so a new upstream release SURFACES as a drift finding instead of needing manual surgery: v7.2.77 threw ~3-min bursts of instant upstream 502s every ~25 min that killed codex-adv renders (Claude Code retries 502s but the companion's render turn does not), and the validated fix was a manual swap to v7.2.113 -- both legs completed clean that night. AUTO-BUMP policy is deliberately SURFACE-ONLY and matches the existing rows' conservatism: apply-drift-bump.sh moves the in-repo pin literal ($Version in cli-proxy-lane.ps1) and synced_base TOGETHER, but NOTHING here restarts the running proxy -- bumping the pin does NOT swap a live instance. The drift leg lands the pin bump as a PR, and the operator runs cli-proxy-lane.ps1 -Install + -Restart (HIMMEL-1451 lifecycle verbs) to actually roll the host. Default tag-mode (highest stable tag, prereleases excluded -- CLIProxyAPI tags are monotonic, so no latest_source override is needed); synced_base lacks the leading 'v' but the guard normalizes both sides before comparing (v7.2.113 tag == 7.2.113 base). tracked_repo is the TRUE upstream (router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI).

entries.name: qmd

fork.note: Drives scripts/upstreams/resync-fork.sh — the REAL repair for this entry, and the reason it deliberately has no `version_pin` (HIMMEL-1323). When upstream tags past synced_base, the honest fix is to rebase the fork's additive delta onto the new upstream base, confirm it is still strictly additive, push the rebased fork, and only THEN move both the SHA pin and synced_base. Bumping synced_base alone would claim a base the fork never rebased onto. Scratch clones only (work_dir, mirroring _qmd_fork_dir's $HOME/.himmel convention) — never the live $HOME/.himmel/qmd-fork install. Nothing is pushed without --push, which itself refuses a conflicted or non-additive rebase.

entries.note: SHA-pinned lib fork yotamleo/qmd (pin in scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh; the additive-delta audit was previously the MANUAL step named in the header). tracked_repo is the TRUE upstream (tobi/qmd). synced_base = the highest upstream STABLE tag the fork carries (fork package.json reads 2.6.3, ahead of upstream's released tags, so this reads CURRENT until upstream tags a version > synced_base). Tier B (reactive) — expected to read BEHIND once upstream cuts 2.5.4+, that IS the signal to re-audit the fork delta. Deliberately carries NO `version_pin`: the in-repo pin is the fork SHA `_qmd_fork_ref` in scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh, not a version, so there is no literal to rewrite — the nightly drift-fix cadence reports it SKIP (manual) and leaves it alone. Auto-bumping synced_base here would mark the fork as carrying an upstream base it has not actually rebased onto, silencing the re-audit signal.
